posts.text:
I once watched a room applaud a metric that couldn't buy a single decision.

Green. Pretty. Useless.

If your numbers can't change what you do this week, you don't have strategy.

You have a dashboard that helps you feel brave.

So I stopped asking "what does the chart say?"

I started asking "what would we do if it moved?"

If the answer is vague, the metric is theater.

Theater is expensive - it eats meetings and pretends it bought clarity.

Pick one ugly number that hurts when it's wrong.

Own it.

Everything else can be wallpaper.

If you've done this exercise and it stung - you're my people.

#Growth #Analytics #Leadership #Product #Operations

The retrieval stack looked healthy.

The policy page was from last quarter.

Your agent is not hallucinating.

Sometimes it's just confidently reading yesterday's truth.

Context rots faster than code.

Docs drift. Policies change. The spreadsheet nobody owns becomes "the source" because it has a link.

If retrieval is your religion, freshness is your discipline.

Expiry dates. Owners. Delete paths.

Boring words - until the wrong paragraph shows up in front of a customer.

I care about systems that know what they don't know.

That's the adult version.

Builders who've seen "almost right" go sideways in public - I would love your war stories.

#AI #RAG #KnowledgeManagement #Engineering #Trust

We wrote the postmortem in passive voice.

"An issue was observed."

Cool.

The system learned nothing.

The fastest teams don't have fewer incidents.

They have less shame about the write-up.

I want the boring facts: what was supposed to be true, what was true, what signal you missed, what you will change before next week.

Blameless doesn't mean consequence-free.

It means the system gets corrected instead of the person getting decorated.

AI makes failures weirder.

So the habit matters more.

If you've ever read a postmortem that sounded like marketing, you know why I'm picky about language.

#Engineering #Culture #Reliability #AI #Leadership

Someone said: "just AI the email."

Okay.

Which email creates precedent?

Which one trains the customer to expect a human?

Which one can commit us while we're in a meeting?

Email is not a file format.

It's a relationship surface.

Automation that treats comms like string replacement creates debt in people's heads.

I'm not saying don't use tools.

I'm saying name the boundary: what can draft, what can send, what must never leave without a human who accepts the tradeoff.

That's not bureaucracy.

That's adulthood.

If you've ever watched scope sneak in through the inbox - same.

#Communication #AI #Sales #Operations #Trust
